title: Company Objectives War Room and Decision Sources Map
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a lightweight operational construct (the 'Company Objectives War Room') and an accompanying Decision Sources Map to reduce ambiguity around who can make scope/priority tradeoffs for company-level OKRs. The output will be a playbook + living map that links each company objective to: owners, escalation paths, primary decision sources (data dashboards, customer signals, legal/regulatory triggers), in-flight initiatives that affect the objective, and a one-page runbook for rapid deconfliction during cross-functional sprints.

Background: Over the past two quarters we've observed recurring delays and rework when competing initiatives change scope or surface conflicts (e.g., runtime-1.18 kernel rollout vs Dedicated autoscaling tuning). PMs, Eng, and Design are spending too much sync time re-establishing priorities rather than executing. Existing OKR artifacts are scattered across Confluence and Linear; there is no single canonical decision-source view.

Goals:
- Reduce cross-team decision latency for company-level OKRs by 40% (measured by time from conflict flagged to decision resolution).
- Provide a single canonical Decision Sources Map that reduces duplicated meetings and clarifies RACI for priority changes.
- Surface high-confidence signals (console latency dashboards, Dedicated capacity shortfall alerts, customer escalations) to a defined war-room rotation.

Scope:
- Company-level OKRs (top 6) and all initiatives directly contributing to those objectives.
- Integrations: Redwood Console dashboards, Support Escalation playbook, Dedicated capacity telemetry, and PRD/Design spec links in Drive.
- Excluded: team-level sprint planning flows or unrelated product OKRs.

Deliverables:
1) Decision Sources Map (single-page living doc in Confluence) mapping objectives -> owners -> decision sources -> escalation path -> active initiatives.
2) War Room playbook (rituals, rotation schedule, decision SLA, meeting template).
3) Dashboard wiring: a pinned Console dashboard that surfaces top 8 signals for war-room triage.
4) Linear workflow templates for triaging objective-level blockers and an associated tag taxonomy.

Success metrics:
- Mean time to decision after a cross-team conflict is flagged drops by 40% within one quarter of rollout.
- 75% of decisions during the first 30 days are made without ad-hoc leadership all-hands (i.e., via war-room cadence).
- Reduction in duplicated escalation threads across Slack and email by 50% (measured by thread counts tagged with objective IDs).

Stakeholders:
- Product: Asha Patel (sponsor), Liam Wong (owner), PM Leads.
- Engineering: Runtime Infra lead, Dedicated infra lead, Console platform.
- Design: Design lead for initiative priority comms.
- GTM: Support and Customer Success leads for customer signals.

Timeline & high-level milestones:
- Week 0-2: Draft Decision Sources Map and War Room playbook (internal draft).
- Week 3: Pilot war-room rotation on 2 objectives (observability, Dedicated capacity).
- Week 4-6: Iterate based on pilot feedback, wire dashboards and Linear templates.
- Week 7: Company-wide rollout and training.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: War room becomes a bottleneck or a bureaucracy. Mitigation: Decision SLA baked in; empower delegated owners with clear guardrails.
- Risk: Signals noise on dashboards leads to churn. Mitigation: Start with top 8 vetted signals, review during pilot and lock cadence for pruning.

Open questions:
- Who will own the short-term rotation schedule (ops or PM)? (Tentative: PM org for first quarter, then rotate to Ops.)
- Are Legal and Security considered primary decision sources or consulted only on escalations?

References and links:
- Confluence draft (Decision Sources Map): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OKR/pages/DSM-2025 (draft)
- Console dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/warroom-proto
- Example PRD: Drive:/Redwood/PRD/okrs-war-room-v1.md
- Github examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/okrs-playbook/pull/142

Acceptance criteria:
- Decision Sources Map created and validated by cross-functional review (PM, Eng, Design, Support).
- War Room pilot executed on 2 objectives and documented outcomes.
- Console dashboard wired and stable for 14 days of pilot traffic.
- Linear templates deployed and adopted by at least 3 active initiatives during pilot.

Notes on implementation approach:
- Use a central Confluence page with a table keyed by objective id (OBJ-01..OBJ-06) to make the map machine-readable for later export to a CSV/JSON for dashboard wiring.
- Keep the war-room ritual to 30 minutes max: 15m signal review, 10m decision/assignments, 5m follow-ups.
- Build a simple Linear automation that attaches the Decision Sources Map link and objective tag when objective-level blockers are filed.
